title: AI assistants and recommender systems as agents of algorithmic socialization
abstract: Context and relevance. In contemporary digital culture, AI assistants and recommender systems increasingly mediate access to information, communication, and cultural models, making it necessary to examine them as new agents of socialization. Objective. The article offers a theoretical and methodological analysis of AI assistants and recommender systems as mediators involved in the shaping of cognitive practices, communicative experience, value orientations, and identity. Hypothesis. Algorithmic systems are assumed to operate not only as technical tools, but also as distinctive mediators of cultural experience that influence the internalization of social norms, patterns of social comparison, and forms of self-presentation. Methods and materials. The study is based on a theoretical-analytical review of the literature. The methodological framework includes conceptual analysis, comparative theoretical analysis, thematic synthesis, and interpretive integration of scholarship in the psychology of socialization, cultural-historical psychology, human—AI interaction, digital ethics, and platform studies. Results. The analysis shows that AI assistants acquire a quasi-social status, shaping communicative expectations, trust, and cognitive habits, while recommender systems participate in constructing social reality, normative understandings, and algorithmically mediated identities. On this basis, the concept of algorithmic socialization is theoretically elaborated. Conclusions. AI should be conceptualized not simply as a tool, but as a new socializing infrastructure and a specific semiotic-technical means that mediates personality development, the formation of higher mental functions, and the internalization of norms in digital culture.
